priorStories.headline: U.S. flight disruptions continue for third day
priorStories.body:
More than 2,300 U.S. flights were canceled and about 7,700 delayed Sunday as airlines continued recovering from Friday’s nationwide ground stop, according to FlightAware figures reported by Reuters.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the cause of the ground stop remained unclear and there was no evidence of a cyberattack or other malicious intent. He said he expected operations to return to normal Monday.

priorStories.headline: Houthis gain control near Bab el-Mandeb Strait
priorStories.body:
Forces aligned with Yemen’s internationally recognized government withdrew from an area overlooking the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, leaving the Iran-aligned Houthis in control, Reuters reported Sunday.

The Saudi-backed forces said they were redeploying from Dhubab Airport and the Bab el-Mandeb area toward Aden. They said their priority was securing Aden and neighboring governorates and strengthening front lines.

candidates.summary: In remarks released for a 5 a.m. EST speech in Milan on November 16, Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr warned that artificial intelligence could amplify financial instability through complex investment financing, synchronized trading, market manipulation and cyberattacks. He called for safeguards protecting consumers and investors and said financial institutions need AI-driven decisions to be controlled, explainable and consistent with law. The remarks did not announce a monetary-policy change.
candidates.title: Fed Governor Barr outlines financial-stability risks from AI

sources.name: Federal Reserve Board — timed speech text

candidates.summary: At a November 16 meeting in Brussels, EU foreign-policy chief Kaja Kallas and several European foreign ministers said discussions with Moscow about Europe's security architecture should await a ceasefire in Ukraine and Russian concessions. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said the EU had approved 145 new sanctions designations that day. Separately, Irish Foreign Minister Helen McEntee said a further sanctions package was being finalized for discussion later in the week; that package was not described as adopted.
candidates.title: EU ministers urge Ukraine ceasefire before broader security talks with Russia

candidates.summary: A State Department notice specifies November 16 as the effective date for a phased pilot accepting selected passport applications online using Form DS–11. Initial eligibility covers certain adults in the United States who previously held passports but cannot use the standard renewal form, and first-time adult applicants using a Certificate of Naturalization as citizenship evidence. The notice does not establish that applications were already being accepted during the observation interval; deployment is described as phased.
candidates.title: Effective date arrives for limited online passport-application pilot

sources.name: U.S. Department of State via Federal Register

candidates.summary: At their November 16 Brussels meeting, EU foreign ministers urged a Ukraine ceasefire and Russian concessions before broader security talks with Moscow. The Council also adopted 145 Russia-related sanctions designations: 12 individuals and 101 entities linked to war financing and the shadow fleet, plus 30 individuals and two entities linked to information manipulation and cyberattacks. Targets included nearly 50 Russian banks and financial institutions, the Social Design Agency and hacker group NoName057(16). A further sanctions package remained under preparation, rather than adopted.
candidates.title: EU adopts Russia-related sanctions as ministers urge ceasefire before security talks

sources.name: Council of the European Union — war-financing sanctions
Council of the European Union — information manipulation and cyber sanctions

candidates.summary: The EU Council on November 16 added four Haitian entities to its Global Human Rights Sanctions Regime. The Council described them as criminal armed groups responsible for grave violations against children in armed conflict, including killings, sexual violence and recruitment of children.
candidates.title: EU sanctions four Haitian armed groups over violations against children

candidates.summary: The European Commission granted unconditional EU merger approval for UniCredit's proposed acquisition of control of Commerzbank on November 16, finding no competition concerns. UniCredit said Federal Reserve approval had also been announced that day. The bank's statement said a final regulatory approval remained outstanding; the clearances did not establish that the acquisition had been completed.
candidates.title: UniCredit receives unconditional EU clearance for Commerzbank acquisition
candidates.geography: European Union; Italy; Germany; United States

candidates.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court on November 16 declined review in Katherine Novotny v. Wes Moore, leaving in place a lower-court ruling upholding Maryland restrictions on carrying firearms in several categories of public places. Justice Clarence Thomas agreed with denying review because the challenge covered multiple statutes with distinct historical questions, while expressing skepticism about the restrictions and support for considering a narrower case. The denial was not a Supreme Court ruling on the constitutional merits.
candidates.title: Supreme Court declines challenge to Maryland public-place gun restrictions

sources.name: Supreme Court of the United States — November 16 order list

candidates.summary: The Commerce Department on November 16 issued a rule aimed at preventing China from accessing advanced U.S. AI chips through remote computing arrangements in third-country data centers, Reuters reported. The rule introduces export-license requirements for advanced chips destined for Singapore, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia and Brazil. The reporting establishes issuance of the rule, but does not establish its effective date.
candidates.title: U.S. issues rule targeting third-country remote access to advanced AI chips
candidates.geography: United States; China; Singapore; Thailand; Malaysia; Indonesia; Brazil

candidates.summary: Institute of International Education survey data released November 16 showed international enrollment at U.S. campuses fell 9% this autumn compared with the previous year. The number of new students entering the United States for the first time fell 15%. These are survey findings about autumn enrollment, not a count of departures or enrollment changes occurring on November 16.
candidates.title: Survey reports decline in international enrollment at U.S. universities

candidates.summary: JPMorgan Chase said November 16 that a software bug in on-premise hardware slowed transaction processing and customer service. The bank said customers could still access accounts and funds and that there was no evidence the issue was cyber-related. It said other banks could experience delays when processing transactions involving Chase. Customers also reported problems at Bank of America, U.S. Bank and Wells Fargo; those reports did not establish separate failures at each bank.
candidates.title: Chase software bug slows transactions and affects payments involving other banks

candidates.summary: United Airlines reported a technology issue affecting departing flights on the afternoon of November 16. In its statement reported by Reuters at 5:23 p.m. EST, the airline said it was troubleshooting the problem; flights already airborne and flights operated by United Express were unaffected. The report did not establish the cause or the number of affected flights.
candidates.title: United reports technology problem affecting departing flights

candidates.summary: U.S. stocks closed lower November 16, with technology shares leading declines. The S&P 500 fell 145.08 points, or 1.9%, to 7,416.59; the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 739.38 points, or 1.4%, to 51,608.17; and the Nasdaq composite lost 626.52 points, or 2.5%, to 24,509.76. It was the S&P 500's third consecutive loss.
candidates.title: U.S. stock indexes fall as technology shares lead declines

candidates.summary: In November 16 remarks for a Federal Reserve conference in San Francisco, Chair Kevin Warsh said emerging technologies could substantially affect economic growth, employment and monetary policy. He outlined possibilities ranging from broadly shared productivity gains to higher unemployment and a slowdown if investment returns disappoint. He said the Fed's role was to prepare for different outcomes rather than advocate for or oppose the technology. The remarks did not announce an interest-rate decision.
candidates.title: Fed Chair Warsh outlines potential economic gains and risks from AI

candidates.summary: Minnesota Attorney General Keith Ellison announced a signed 10-year oversight agreement with Sutter Health and Allina Health on November 16, completing his office's review of their proposed combination. Commitments include $2.15 billion in investment over five years, preservation of core services for five years, and continued reproductive and gender care subject to applicable law. The agreement also protects collective-bargaining commitments. Completion of the attorney general's review did not establish that the transaction had closed.
candidates.title: Minnesota concludes Sutter-Allina review with investment and service commitments

candidates.summary: The COP31 presidency released an initial draft cover-decision text on November 16 to support further negotiations. Its accompanying note said the draft reflected submissions and delegation consultations, not consensus, and included proposals opposed by some parties. All elements remained open for discussion, including whether to retain them. Publication of the draft did not constitute adoption of a climate agreement.
candidates.title: COP31 presidency releases initial negotiating draft without consensus

sources.name: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
